A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, research questions and experiments. Both contain 67 readable pages, including appendices A–H; equations, text and all 35 figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on sparse recovery, matrix recovery, modular addition, nonlinear teacher–student learning and MNIST, including results throughout appendices D–H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including training trajectories, recovery errors and classification accuracies in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The regularized objectives, model parameterizations and subgradient, projected-gradient and proximal procedures remain unchanged. The expanded analysis of regularized updates in Theorem C.25 concerns an existing procedure, not a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same sparse-recovery, matrix-sensing/completion, modular-addition, nonlinear teacher–student, Sobolev-training and MNIST coverage. No evaluated task or data scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same regularizer comparisons, iterative methods and convex-programming alternatives. The added Tibshirani citation supports an existing convergence bound rather than introducing an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Reported experimental settings remain unchanged, including addition modulo 97 with 40% training data and MNIST with 1,000 training examples. Optimizers, initialization rules, parameter sweeps and error criteria are retained; revised theoretical step-size conditions are not experimental protocol changes.

E4.justification: The same analyses of regularization strength, learning rate, depth, sample size, sparsity, coherence and optimization trajectories remain in Sections 3–4 and appendices D–H. Relocated appendix figures do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed summaries, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The revision does not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figures 1–35 retain the same plotted results, and the associated empirical values and findings are unchanged. The reported effects of regularization, depth and coherence are preserved without added or removed result entries.

T1.justification: Theorem C.25 is substantially extended from unregularized gradient descent to regularized updates, with new gradient-dominance conditions, convergence expressions, proof and parameter analysis. Other revisions change the generalized CL definition and first-phase bounds, replace equality with an inequality in Theorem 3.4, and add principal-angle derivations in C.6. These are substantive mathematical changes, not merely notation edits.

C1.justification: The introduction adds sufficient model complexity to the conditions for its broad grokking claim, alongside sufficient training data. The abstract, principal contributions and conclusion otherwise retain the same scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies applicability through model complexity and explains that local smoothness follows within the CL analysis, whereas the PL analysis assumes smoothness. Existing interpretations of depth, coherence and failures of the ℓ2-norm indicator remain intact.

D1.justification: The experimental subgradient choices, initialization rules, hyperparameters, PyTorch/Adam and CVXPY information, and code-access link are retained. Removing a redundant sign-subgradient sentence does not remove the experimentally used rule, which remains stated in C.4.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tibshirani (2015) for the proximal-gradient bound and removes the Bauschke and Combettes (2009) reference. The extensive related-work appendix and broader positioning relative to earlier grokking research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction and mathematical-exposition rewrites, terminology refinements, and affiliation and acknowledgment edits. The main narrative and section sequence remain stable; added mathematical substance does not constitute wholesale restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds running-title headers, adjusts equation presentation and relocates existing figures, including Figures 19, 20, 23 and 30. Figures 14–15 receive small caption corrections. The plotted contents and overall visual organization are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 usefully clarifies definitions and corrects Theorem 3.4, but its expanded PL analysis introduces mathematical errors. Equation (54) incorrectly expands the gradient cross-term, and the subsequent feasibility analysis reverses an inequality, wrongly declaring μ < 2L infeasible. These new defects weaken the added convergence guarantee and outweigh the limited corrections and exposition gains; the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
